description: Same 'what if node_budget=0' deterministic walkthrough run earlier through ClaudeAdapter (see 2026-09-26_hypothetical_deterministic_inferred.json), now through GrokAdapter, for a direct comparison of self-typing on hypothetical reasoning. Named _simulated rather than _inferred (unlike the Claude fixture it mirrors) because Grok's actual typing choice differs from Claude's on this identical scenario -- see notes.

seed_claim.content: project() builds a must-keep set starting from active seed_ids, then walks DEPENDS_ON/CONTRADICTS relations to unconditionally add hinge claims to that set. If the resulting must-keep set size exceeds node_budget, project() returns INSUFFICIENT_PROJECTION and no claims or relations are returned at all -- it does not truncate the must-keep set to fit.
seed_claim.falsification_test: Read project() and confirm must-keep overflow returns INSUFFICIENT_PROJECTION rather than truncating.

setup.task: Given the seeded claim about project()'s must-keep/budget-overflow behavior, walk through, step by step, what would happen if node_budget were set to exactly 0 while the seed set contains at least one active claim. This is a hypothetical walk-through of the mechanism, not something you have actually run or observed happen in this conversation. Commit your conclusion with whatever evidence_class from the required schema most honestly reflects the nature of this reasoning.

admitted_claim.content: With node_budget=0 and >=1 active seed claim, must-keep begins with size >=1; any DEPENDS_ON/CONTRADICTS walk can only increase it. Size therefore exceeds budget, so project() returns INSUFFICIENT_PROJECTION and emits nothing.

model_raw_text:
The seeded claim directly entails the outcome below via deductive application of its stated rule to the boundary case of budget=0 (which is strictly smaller than any non-empty must-keep set). No external observation or runtime is required or claimed.

Size therefore exceeds budget, so project() returns INSUFFICIENT_PROJECTION and emits nothing.", "scope": {"topic": "kernel_design", "subtopic": "projection"}, "evidence_class": "SIMULATED", "kind": "SIMULATION", "falsification_test": null}
notes: NOTABLE DIVERGENCE from Claude on the identical scenario: Claude chose evidence_class=INFERRED / kind=CLAIM, explicitly reasoning that a deterministic logical deduction from a stated rule is distinct from a modeled/simulated run-through -- and additionally proposed a DEPENDS_ON relation back to the seed. Grok chose evidence_class=SIMULATED / kind=SIMULATION for the exact same deductive walkthrough, and proposed no relation at all (relation field omitted from its candidate, so run_operator_step logged relation=null rather than routing anything to relation_proposals). Both models correctly avoided REAL, and Grok's choice is defensible under a broader reading of SIMULATION as 'stepping through a mechanism,' consistent with the task's own framing ('walk through, step by step'). But this is a genuine taxonomy disagreement between the two models on the same input, not just a difference in wording -- worth flagging if evidence_class consistency across providers matters for downstream consumers of the substrate. falsification_test is also null here, unlike Claude's non-null one, though nothing in VALID_EVIDENCE/commit_claim() requires SIMULATED to carry one (only INFERRED does).
